reading.body:
Anna Hegreness is named on 13 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm for one client, Google Client Services LLC, and all naming bills from 2025 or later.

The structure is narrow. Thirteen AI filings, one firm, one client. A single lobbyist carrying one company's AI interests through one shop is the concentrated form of the arrangement, and the count of 26 points is mostly the bill list rather than a widening set of clients or firms.

The bills run across both chambers, with House and Senate numbers interleaved through the list. That spread matters for AI because the rules that will shape data centers, model deployment, and procurement are being written in many separate vehicles at once, not one. A client retaining coverage across that many bills is buying presence in the committee rooms where power and permitting language gets attached, which is where compute buildout timelines are actually set.

What this does not show is position. The data records that a bill was named on a filing, not what was said about it, whether the client supports or opposes it, or whether any of it changed an outcome. It also covers one lobbyist and one client, so it says nothing about the scale of AI lobbying overall.
